newsitem.title: THAILAND: N.Korea food shortages seen worsening in 1997.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea food shortages seen worsening in 1997.

text.p: The food shortage in North Korea will worsen considerably this year and require large-scale international assistance to ensure minimum needs are met, the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said in a report.

Heavy rainfall and floods in late July caused widespread damage, particularly in key agricultural zones, including North and South Hwanghae provinces, Kangwon and Kaesong municipality, the Rome-based FAO said in report obtained by Reuters.
These areas produced some 60 percent of North Korea's food grain, especially rice, it added.

"Two successive years of floods have undoubtedly set back agriculture and significantly compounded underlying food production problems in the country," said the report based on an FAO/World Food Programme mission to the country.
The net output of milled rice and maize available for 1996/97 was estimated at only 2.84 million tonnes, leaving an overall import requirement of more than two million tonnes, the report said.
The underlying food production problems cited in the report included steep declines in fertiliser production and imports of essential materials such as fertilisers, pesticides, fuel and spare parts.
"(North Korea's) capacity to import food commercially is highly constrained by a lack of foreign exchange, large international debts and virtually no access to credit," the report said.
Under these conditions, the country would have to resort to bartering badly needed raw materials for grain as it did last year, the report said.
Pyongyang's official news agency said on Wednesday a delegation from U.S. grain giant Cargill Inc had arrived in North Korea for talks about a food barter deal.
Earlier this month, Washington granted Cargill permission to supply up to two million tonnes of grain to North Korea through barter trade.
